group: Revised Cardiac Risk Index for Pre-Operative Risk
question:
Patient note:
A 74-year-old man was evaluated late this morning in the ambulatory pre-admission center at the request of general surgery three days before an elective open right inguinal herniorrhaphy with mesh that is expected to last roughly one hour and require a single night of observation on the surgical ward for pain control; no major blood loss or prolonged pneumoperitoneum is anticipated, and the surgeon has not scheduled postoperative critical-care monitoring. The patient arrived unaccompanied, walked the length of the corridor at a leisurely pace carrying his coat, and sat without appearing winded, yet he related that over the last two years his activity tolerance has declined: he still tends his backyard vegetable garden but now needs to rest on a patio chair after pushing the mower for only ten minutes, sleeps propped on two pillows to avoid breathlessness, and has been awakened twice in the past month with abrupt nocturnal dyspnea that improved after he sat on the edge of the bed. Three months ago he was hospitalized for lower-extremity edema and bibasilar crackles; intravenous furosemide brought five kilograms of weight loss, and echocardiography at that admission demonstrated a dilated left ventricle with an ejection fraction of 35 % and mild functional mitral regurgitation without regional wall-motion abnormalities. He has never experienced substernal pressure, jaw or arm discomfort, exertional angina, or undergone coronary angiography, and a nuclear perfusion study performed last winter for dyspnea showed no reversible defects. His current cardiology regimen—taken faithfully this morning—comprises carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, sacubitril–valsartan 24/26 mg twice daily, bumetanide 1 mg each morning, spironolactone 25 mg nightly, and low-dose aspirin for primary prevention; sodium intake is limited to approximately 1.5 g per day, and he weighs himself daily, calling the clinic if he gains more than two pounds in 24 hours. Hypertension diagnosed in midlife is controlled with amlodipine 5 mg and has produced no known end-organ complications; he denies diabetes, stroke, transient visual loss, focal weakness, claudication, or prior carotid imaging. Past operations include appendectomy in his twenties and uncomplicated cataract extraction two years ago. He quit cigarettes thirty years earlier after a 40-pack-year exposure, drinks red wine on holidays, and has never used illicit substances. Review of systems is negative for palpitations, syncope, hemoptysis, abdominal pain, weight loss, fever, or night sweats. After five minutes seated his vital signs were: blood pressure 114/68 mm Hg in the right arm, pulse 72 beats per minute and regular, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 98 % breathing ambient air, oral temperature 36.6 °C, and body mass index 27 kg/m². He appeared euvolemic; jugular venous pulsation was 5 cm above the sternal angle at 45°, carotid upstrokes were brisk without bruits, and the point of maximal impulse was laterally displaced in the sixth interspace. Cardiac auscultation revealed a soft S3 and a grade 1/6 apical holosystolic murmur consistent with the documented valvular insufficiency; no rubs were heard. Lungs were clear centrally with faint late-inspiratory crackles at both bases that did not clear with coughing. Abdomen was soft with a visible right groin bulge that protruded when he coughed and reduced easily with gentle pressure; no organomegaly or ascites was present. Extremities exhibited trace pitting edema to the ankles with 2+ dorsalis pedis pulses bilaterally, warm skin, and intact capillary refill. Neurologic screen showed alert mentation, intact cranial nerves, full strength, normal sensation, and a steady heel-to-toe gait. Pre-operative laboratory studies drawn one hour before the visit documented hemoglobin 13.8 g/dL, white blood cells 6.0 × 10⁹/L, platelets 248 × 10⁹/L, sodium 137 mmol/L, potassium 4.1 mmol/L, chloride 101 mmol/L, bicarbonate 24 mmol/L, blood urea nitrogen 18 mg/dL, and a serum creatinine of 1.11 mg/dL, yielding an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 67 mL/min/1.73 m²; fasting glucose was 102 mg/dL, liver enzymes and coagulation profile were within reference intervals. A 12-lead electrocardiogram obtained today showed normal sinus rhythm at 70 beats per minute with nonspecific intraventricular conduction delay and no ST-segment deviations or Q waves compared with a tracing six months earlier. Upright posterior–anterior chest radiograph revealed a mildly enlarged cardiac silhouette with clear lung fields and no pleural effusions. Airway examination by anesthesia demonstrated Mallampati class II view, inter-incisor distance of 4 cm, and full cervical extension. He has been instructed to continue the beta-blocker and renin-angiotensin-neprilysin inhibitor through the morning of surgery, omit the loop diuretic on the day of operation to avoid intravascular depletion, maintain nothing by mouth after midnight except clear liquids until two hours before arrival, and bring his home weight log to the hospital. Mechanical thromboprophylaxis, incentive spirometry, and early ambulation were reviewed in detail; after questions were answered he expressed understanding and willingness to proceed with the scheduled hernia repair.

Question: What is the patient's score of the Revised Cardiac Risk Index for Pre-Operative Risk? You should use the patient's medical values and health status when they were first admitted to the hospital prior to any treatment.
solution:
The Revised Cardiac Risk Index (RCRI) assigns 1 point for each of six preoperative risk factors:
- High-risk surgery (intraperitoneal, intrathoracic, or suprainguinal vascular): open inguinal hernia repair is not in these categories → 0.
- Ischemic heart disease: no documented coronary disease or angina; perfusion testing showed no reversible defects → 0.
- History of heart failure: prior hospitalization for congestion, EF 35%, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea → 1.
- Cerebrovascular disease: no history of stroke or TIA → 0.
- Preoperative insulin therapy: no diabetes or insulin use → 0.
- Preoperative creatinine >2.0 mg/dL: creatinine 1.11 mg/dL → 0.
Sum: 0 + 0 + 1 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 1.
Final answer: 1
